clue.text: Chemical used by cook a lot badly discoloured him

definitions.text: Chemical used by cook a lot

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and out of order, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: fourteen letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A careless chef has spilt some chemical on himself and stained his skin.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'a lot': common salt is the chemical a cook reaches for constantly. 'Badly discoloured' reads as one phrase about him, but only 'badly' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium chloride is the scientific name for table salt, the seasoning used constantly in kitchens.

clue.text: Second best doctor accepting a temporary solution

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the doctor holds the next word inside

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
top means best, as in top quality
a GP is a general practitioner, the family doctor in Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner-up physician grudgingly takes on a short-term fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second best' looks like one phrase meaning runner-up, but it splits into two pieces. The A goes inside GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is something used for the time being until a proper replacement is found.

clue.text: The elite, in fact, ride all over the place

indicators.note: scattered in every direction, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: fifteen letters of fodder, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Members of the upper class go riding wherever they please.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The' looks like an ordinary opening word of the sentence, but it is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the word 'the' is called the definite article, as opposed to the indefinite 'a'.

clue.text: Part of skeleton concealed by artful natives

indicators.note: something concealed by the following words sits tucked inside them, running across the gap

parts.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Cunning locals have hidden a bone somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the human forearm, a part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Keen to embrace that female in bright red

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap the arms around, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, so to cry
the pronoun for a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: Someone eager to hug a woman dressed in vivid scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' reads as eager, but here it is the verb meaning to lament loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry is the name of a vivid red colour, after the fruit.

clue.text: Identified as beautiful woman in youth

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a lad is a young man
a belle is a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A beauty is recognised among young people.
explanation.definitionFit: To be labelled as something is to be tagged or classed as it, so identified as.

clue.text: Logical about European line, concerning how connections are made

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for logical surrounds the next pieces

parts.note: rational means reasoned and logical
E is the abbreviation for European
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A sensible remark about a European line of reasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The E and L go together just after the first letter of the word for logical.
explanation.definitionFit: Relational describes relations, the ways in which things are linked to each other.

clue.text: Greater variety I had turned up, covering poet's work

indicators.note: in a down entry, something covering another sits above it, so it comes first
in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
versification is the craft of writing verse

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of having raised the range of a poet's output.
explanation.definitionFit: Diversification is the process of branching out, which produces more variety.

clue.text: Run into healthy male in New York area

indicators.note: one thing put into another sits inside it

parts.note: hale means in robust health
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A jogger bumps into a fit man somewhere in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlem is a neighbourhood in the north of Manhattan, New York City.

clue.text: Crime of person who sells property of others

parts.note: taken as written

parts.words: person who sells property of others
parts.note: a fence is a dealer in stolen goods

explanation.surface: It reads as a description of the offence committed by a dealer in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like it ties the definition to the rest, but it supplies its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of the law, a crime.

clue.text: State of some South Americans, mostly furious when constricted?

indicators.note: being constricted means being squeezed by something wrapped around it

parts.note: the question mark hints at a constrictor snake doing the constricting

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: livid means very angry

explanation.surface: It describes the angry mood of some South Americans who feel hemmed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like mood, but it is a country. The constrictor implied by the question mark is a boa, a snake that squeezes its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolivia is a sovereign nation, a state, whose people are South Americans.

clue.text: Team is gambling, having dropped centre half

indicators.note: dropping the centre half means losing the middle part of the word

parts.note: gaming is betting on games of chance

explanation.surface: A football side bets heavily after leaving out its central defender.
explanation.walkthrough: A centre half is a football position, a central defender; here it means the middle two letters of six.
explanation.definitionFit: A gang is a group of people working together, so a team.

clue.text: Involving more than two parties, subsequently, in case

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: a court case is a trial
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: A lawsuit later turns out to involve several parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Trilateral means having three sides, so involving three parties, more than two.

clue.text: Can let room rebuilt in Mediterranean resort

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a different form

parts.note: ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A hotel can rent out a renovated room at a seaside holiday spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Monte Carlo is the famous resort district of Monaco on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Everything contained in spam etc wrong for customer

indicators.note: everything contained in each word means all its inner letters, leaving out the ends

parts.note: the inner letters, once the ends are dropped
the single inner letter
the inner letters, once the ends are dropped

explanation.surface: Junk email and the like gets everything wrong for the shopper.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase looks like it describes the contents of junk mail, but it asks for the interior of each of the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop, restaurant or business.

clue.text: Within firms it openly reversed corrupt employment practice

indicators.note: the run of letters is read from right to left
within means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the end of the first word, all of the second, the start of the third

explanation.surface: Firms are openly accused of crooked hiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Openly' suggests nothing is concealed, yet it holds part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotism is favouritism in giving jobs to relatives, a corrupt way of hiring.

clue.text: Shared income cut, and money doubly so

indicators.note: a cut word loses its tail, here its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: doubly so means cut twice over, so two letters come off the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple's joint earnings are reduced, and their savings twice as much.
explanation.definitionFit: Things held in common belong jointly to more than one person, so they are shared.

clue.text: Without energy, having nothing to eat? Just the opposite

definitions.note: the definition leans on the wordplay: the opposite of having nothing to eat

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: fasting means going without food
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone tired and starving, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like it means lacking, but it means outside: the word for going hungry wraps around E. The result is its opposite, eating lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasting means eating a large, lavish meal, the reverse of going hungry.

clue.text: Some beef, lamb, etc cooked in dramatic way

indicators.note: some of the following words means only a portion of their letters

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, punctuation ignored

explanation.surface: Meats such as beef and lamb are prepared with theatrical flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé food is doused in spirit and set alight, a showy way of cooking it.

clue.text: Is concerned about one problem seen in oral examination

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: someone who cares is concerned
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A student worries about a single difficulty in a spoken exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral examination' suggests a spoken test; it is a dentist looking in a mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is tooth decay, which a dentist spots when checking the mouth.

clue.text: Create colony around a port on Pacific

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes outside the other

parts.note: to settle a land is to colonise it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pioneers found a colony near a harbour on the Pacific coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is a major seaport city in Washington State on the Pacific coast of the USA.

clue.text: Power needed in Asian city for site of ancient sanctuary

indicators.note: something needed in a place goes inside it

parts.note: Delhi is the city in India
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An Indian city needs electricity for an old temple site.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi in Greece was home to the shrine of Apollo and its famous oracle.

clue.text: Edible flower heads are so thick, oddly

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters come out in a new order

parts.note: ten letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Some edible flowers are strangely dense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like it might ask for alternate letters, but here it signals a rearrangement of all ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Globe artichokes are the unopened flower buds of a thistle-like plant, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Source of wool one left out initially for Eastern monk

indicators.note: out at the start means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: the llama is an Andean animal kept for its wool
L is the abbreviation for left; one of them is lost

explanation.surface: A wool-bearing animal is left out for a Tibetan holy man.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a spiritual teacher in Tibetan Buddhism, a monk of the East.

clue.text: Greek deity in Egyptian port set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Suez is the port at the head of the Gulf of Suez

explanation.surface: A statue of a Greek god is erected in an Egyptian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was king of the gods of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Coarse material in book youngster returned

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: Mark is a book of the New Testament
a cub is a young animal, or a junior scout

explanation.surface: Rough cloth is found in a volume a child brought back.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckram is a stiff, coarse cloth used in bookbinding and to stiffen clothes.

clue.text: Forecast in proclamation from publicity department?

parts.note: PR is public relations, a firm's publicity department
an edict is an official proclamation

explanation.surface: A prediction appears in a press release from the PR office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From' places the publicity department's letters before the proclamation's.
explanation.definitionFit: To predict is to say in advance what will happen, to forecast.

clue.text: Initial survey, study set in period of cultural renewal

indicators.note: something set in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the Renaissance was the European revival of art and learning
to con is an old word for to study or learn

explanation.surface: A first overview of a study set in the age of artistic rebirth.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconnaissance is preliminary exploration of ground, a first survey before acting.
